## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C IPO and TRA execution

- 2017-10-12: S-1/A files the form-of TRA as Exhibit 10.1
- 2017-11-01: TRA executed at IPO closing between Funko, Inc., FAH, LLC, and the Continuing Equity Owners (ACON, Fundamental Capital, and certain officers/directors)
- 2018-03-19: Executed TRA filed as Exhibit 10.25 to the FY2017 10-K

#### Valuation-allowance write-down

- 2023-08-03: Q2 2023 10-Q records a full valuation allowance on deferred tax assets, reducing the TRA liability from $109.2M to $9.6M and recognizing a $99.6M gain
- 2024-03-07: FY2023 10-K confirms no future tax benefits are expected to be realized under the TRA; status set to economically extinguished but contract in force
- 2025-03-13: FY2024 10-K records a catch-up TRA payment of $8.96M; year-end recorded liability $0.5M against a $99.6M gross outstanding balance

## Explanation

Funko's TRA originated at its November 1, 2017 Up-C IPO, obligating the public company to pay 85% of cumulative net realized tax benefits from Section 754 basis step-ups arising from future exchanges of FAH common units for Class A stock. The contract has never been amended or terminated; the May 2022 TCG secondary purchase was a Class A stock transfer at the holder level and did not add a TRA party. In Q2 2023, Funko recorded a full valuation allowance on its deferred tax assets and concluded TRA payments were no longer probable, writing the recorded liability down from $109.2M to $9.6M and recognizing a $99.6M gain; subsequent periods have kept the recorded liability near zero ($120k at year-end 2025) while the gross undiscounted obligation has continued to grow with each new exchange ($102.5M at year-end 2025). See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
